ios.desc:
The bird never moves. The paper does.

PaperFlip is a one-finger folding game. Hold to crease the sheet inward. Release and it springs back. Every wall has a notch above the crease and a matching one below. Fold until those notches meet the crease — then the paper crane slips through.

Fold too little and you hit the wall.
Fold too far and the paper crushes you.

That is the whole game. Timing, not tapping.

HOW TO PLAY
• Hold to fold the paper toward the center crease
• Release to unfold
• Match the fold to each gap as walls slide past
• Stay out of the red — overfolding is a crush

WHY IT FEELS DIFFERENT
You are not flapping a bird. You are folding the world around it. Every wall asks for a different depth. Some need a deep crease, some need you to let go instantly. Perfect alignment is a few percent of error. Miss that window and you still live — until you don’t.

FEATURES
• One control: hold and release
• Endless run with a rising difficulty curve
• Perfect and close-call feedback
• Personal best marked on the paper
• Optional rewarded revive and double score
• One-time Remove Ads purchase
• No account. No login. Scores stay on your device.

Fold the paper, not the bird.

quotes.text:
I made a tiny iPhone arcade game around one idea: what if Flappy Bird, but the bird never moves — and you fold the paper instead?

Hold anywhere to fold the sheet inward, release to spring it back. Each wall has mirrored notches above and below the crease. Fold just enough so they meet and the crane slips through. Under-fold and you hit the wall; over-fold and the paper crushes you.

It's one verb (hold/release), offline, no account. Perfects, combos, close calls, and a ghost line of your best score. Free with ads; optional one-time Remove Ads.

Built in Swift for iOS 17+. Happy to talk about the feel tuning (fold warp, crush warning, haptics) or anything that felt unfair.

App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/paperflip/id6807705987
Site: https://abiaolhb.github.io/PaperFlipHtml/

Curious what tripped you up in the first 30 seconds.
